label: D1 after unrewarded common a2->S2, largest when belief moderately favours S2
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * belief_lo**2 ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) * (in_rew == 0) * (np.abs(belief_lo) < 1.5)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (zero at GO/D2). Magnitude is driven almost entirely by the previous trial being a2 -> S2 common, unrewarded (residual +0.33 vs about -0.04 for every other pattern; this indicator alone gives dev R^2 0.30 beyond timing). Within those trials it is graded by the ideal-observer belief: binned weights are about 0.78 for P(S1 good) 0.1-0.3, 0.53 for 0.3-0.7, 0.32 above 0.7, i.e. strongest when the agent had reason to think S2 was good and S2 then failed to pay (a quadratic in belief_lo brings it to about 0.41). It is weaker when the trial before was also unrewarded (-0.16). For a window first trial (previous trial outside the window) with no reward and an uncertain belief there is a small extra term. belief_cover adds nothing. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.43, against an all-cue ceiling of 0.44 and an all-observed ceiling of 0.36. The earlier model-based fit used the policy decile (0.12 alone), so using observed quantities only loses little. What is left over is mostly trial-to-trial variation in peak size (0.7-1.4) on matching a2 S2 u trials that these cues do not predict.
